A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Who&When study and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A-G. Reordered sections and the rasterized annotation guidelines can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original failure-attribution experiments, including method comparisons, context-length and tolerance analyses, hybrid-method results, and appendix reasoning-prompt and reasoning-model evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results in Tables 1-4 and the experimental figures, including reasoning-model evaluations in Section 4.8 and the prompt ablation in Appendix B.1.

M1.justification: The three attribution procedures and the hybrid pipeline in Section 4.7 are unchanged. Algorithm pseudocode moves from Appendix B to Appendix A, and Appendix G retains the same prompt templates.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 184 tasks from 127 systems covering GAIA and AssistantBench. Changing 'entire GAIA' to 'rest of the GAIA' reconciles wording with the 30 hand-crafted-system GAIA cases already specified in v1 and Table 5; it does not establish changed coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 3, and 4 retain the same comparison methods, including the random baseline, three attribution methods, hybrid comparison, and two-method reasoning-model evaluation. Newly cited reward-model research is not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The reported sample counts, ground-truth conditions, metrics, evaluated models, and iteration limits remain unchanged. Explicit context-length bin boundaries and the reasoning experiment's hand-crafted-system scope document existing evaluations rather than revise their protocols.

E4.justification: The reasoning-prompt ablation moves from Appendix A.1 to B.1 without changing its evidence. Context-length, tolerance, prediction-distance, aggregate-agent, and hybrid analyses are retained, as is the dataset example; no new robustness analysis or case study appears.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same annotation-uncertainty and disagreement reporting. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for attribution accuracies, and the existing distribution summaries are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched tables and plots retain their numerical results and findings. For example, Table 3 still reports hybrid accuracy of 57.02% at agent level and 12.28% at step level, while Table 4 retains 13.79% step accuracy for o1 with step-by-step attribution. Relocation and axis-label edits introduce no new results.

T1.justification: The system formalization, intervention-based decisive-error definition, earliest-error criterion, and token-cost derivations in Equations (1)-(8) are unchanged. The added sentence identifying the turn-based protocol restates an assumption already explicit in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: formulating automated multi-agent failure attribution, introducing Who&When, and evaluating three methods that expose the task's difficulty. Moving reasoning-model evidence into the main text does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations concerning context access, precise step localization, longer-log difficulty, aggregate attribution, hybrid computational cost, and limited benefits from stronger reasoning models. No substantive applicability boundary or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 newly specifies the five context-length ranges: 5-17, 19-29, 31-49, 51-91, and 93-130 steps. Section 4.8 explicitly identifies hand-crafted systems as the reasoning-model evaluation subset. These improve documentation; prompt templates, hyperparameter defaults, and the repository link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a focused Reward Models discussion, including Math-Shepherd and ProcessBench, distinguishing single-LLM step verification from multi-agent failure attribution. It also adds Nemotron-Research-Tool-N1 and removes several judge and safety citations, while retaining the original overall novelty framing.

P1.justification: The reasoning-model discussion moves from Appendix A.2 to Section 4.8, and the algorithm and additional-experiment appendices exchange order. Local grammar corrections, a shortened impact statement, and affiliation/publication-text additions accompany these changes; most prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 moves into the main text, table spacing and placement change, and Figure 8 switches to integer agent-count ticks. Figure 10 becomes a smaller raster image containing the same guidelines. v3 also introduces placeholder running headers; the displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit length-bin ranges and reasoning-test subset improve experimental documentation, while the new reward-model discussion clarifies the relationship to prior step-error detection research. These are modest gains with unchanged empirical support, partly offset by the smaller rasterized annotation guidelines and placeholder running headers.
